title: Web Components
description: <minerva-button>: a framework-agnostic custom element built with Lit, usable in plain HTML, React, Vue or any other framework.

what.title: What it is
what.p1: @minerva/lib-web-components packages Minerva components as standard custom elements. Importing the package once registers them with the browser; after that they behave like built-in HTML tags in any page or framework.
what.p2: The elements render into a shadow root, so their internal styles cannot leak into your page (or be broken by it). They are configured with HTML attributes and emit regular DOM events such as click.

html.title: Usage in HTML
html.text: Load the package as an ES module (through your bundler), then use the tags anywhere in the document. Boolean attributes such as loading or disabled are on when present.

react.title: Usage in React
react.text: Import the package once for its side effect, and reference the bundled typings to type-check attributes in JSX. onClick and other DOM events work as usual; use aria-label (with a dash) for the accessible name.
react.booleans: React 18 sets attributes on custom elements as strings, so loading={false} becomes loading="false", which still counts as present. Pass true or undefined (e.g. loading={saving || undefined}) to toggle boolean attributes. React 19 sets them as properties and accepts plain booleans.

other.title: Vue and other frameworks
other.text: Any framework that renders HTML can use the elements. In Vue, declare minerva-* tags as custom elements so the compiler doesn't try to resolve them as Vue components, and bind null to remove a boolean attribute. Angular needs CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA; Svelte, Solid and Lit work without configuration.

theming.title: Theming
theming.text: The button reads its own CSS custom properties (--primary-color, --primary-hover, --error-color, ...) with defaults declared on the element, so it does not automatically follow lib-core's ConfigProvider theme. Set the variables on the element, or in a rule that targets it, to match your design:

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.text: The element renders a native <button> inside its shadow root, so it is focusable and keyboard-operable. The aria-label attribute is forwarded to that button; set it on icon-only buttons. While loading, the button sets aria-busy and ignores clicks; disabled buttons are not focusable.

basic.title: Basic usage
basic.description: Import the package once, then use <minerva-button> like any element. React's onClick works as with native elements.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: Nine variants: primary, secondary, success, warning, error, info, ghost, retry and back.

sizes-shapes.title: Sizes and shapes
sizes-shapes.description: Four sizes (tiny to large) and four shapes. Icon-only circle buttons need an aria-label.

states.title: States
states.description: loading shows a spinner and blocks clicks; disabled and active are boolean attributes too. In React 18 pass true or undefined, never false.

wc_ButtonProps.variant: Visual style of the button (reflected to the variant attribute).
wc_ButtonProps.loading: Shows a spinner instead of the content and blocks clicks; sets aria-busy.
wc_ButtonProps.active: Renders the button in its pressed / active style.
wc_ButtonProps.ariaLabel: Accessible label forwarded to the inner <button>; set it with the aria-label attribute. Required for icon-only buttons.
